hypothesis: If eggs are never oblate, no bird species has a typical egg wider than it is long.
pass_criterion: Among species in the dataset, none has a mean egg breadth exceeding mean egg length by more than 2% (measurement tolerance), so the maximum species mean breadth/length ratio is at most 1.02.
fail_criterion: Five or more species have a mean breadth/length ratio above 1.05, i.e. clearly oblate eggs.
interpretation: 'Prolate' means length exceeds breadth. 'Oblate/discoidal' means breadth exceeds length. The test uses species-level mean egg dimensions (and ellipticity or asymmetry where given) from a published egg-shape dataset covering 955 species. Hard-shelled eggs of birds are the scope tested; reptile eggs are outside this dataset.

dataset.name: Data from: The evolution of egg shape in birds: Evolutionary constraints and adaptations
dataset.why_it_fits: The Dryad record has an egg shape file for 955 extant bird species plus oviduct, pelvis and phylogeny files. The egg length, breadth and shape-index fields are used to compute breadth/length ratios.
